text:
alex_k: handing off the KV eviction + routing fallback incident — paging still active. root cause summary: heavy prefix churn + one EU routing cluster hit high CPU after auto-fallback from a capacity-constrained zone. some traffic spilled to other regions and bumped request queues.

maria_s: current state — alerts: KV eviction rate elevated (3x baseline), routing queue depth > 200, p99 latency for /v1/generate ~ 1.2s (normal ~350ms). customers impacted: a subset of hosted API tenants in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 showing timeouts. PD incident INC-4721 open.

oncall-bot: [INCIDENT] INC-4721 created by maria_s; severity: SEV2. Pager duty notifications sent to on-call rotation. Links: https://pd.example/INC-4721

sam: acked. taking primary. quick question: do we know which model shards are causing the eviction surges or is this routing imbalance? any hotspots in KV-store nodes?

alex_k: KV telemetry shows three nodes with spike in mem pressure and frequent LRU evictions. suspecting a small set of heavy prefixes bypassing cache. routing histogram shows a jump in cross-region routing events after eu-west AZ failure at 02:12.

jordan_p: I've started a temporary routing rule to bias eu traffic to eu-central warm pool (rule-id: route-temporary-2309). watch for additional load there. command I ran:
```
redwoodctl routing update --region eu-west --failover-target eu-central --weight 0.8 --meta incident=INC-4721
```
Effect: reduced cross-region latency but increased load on eu-central proxies.

lee: mitigation in progress: 1) added 2x proxies in eu-central (k8s scale); 2) lowered batch target on hosting cluster for models with heavy tail; 3) reduced client-side max concurrency for affected tenants via quota override. Commands:
```
kubectl -n routing scale deploy routing-proxy-eu-central --replicas=6
redwoodctl config set batch.target=8 --selector=tenant:high-tail
redwoodctl quota set tenant-42 concurrency=10 --temp --expires=30m
```
Initial results: routing queue depth dropped ~30% after scaling, p99 latency dropping to ~850ms.

maria_s: note for handoff: runbook section is "Routing fallback spillover" (link): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/ROUTE-FALLBACK. main playbook items: evaluate routing weights, scale proxies, apply temporary tenant throttles, consider model variant fallback (quantized variant) if GPU pressure persists.

sam: I'm picking up primary. immediate actions I'll run during my shift: 1) verify eviction script on hotspot nodes (eviction-rebalance.sh), 2) instrument a KV metric to track prefix churn, 3) coordinate with infra to provision 1 additional shard if evictions continue.

alex_k: eviction-rebalance.sh path:
```
ssh kv-node-12
sudo /opt/redwood/bin/eviction-rebalance.sh --threshold 0.75 --dry-run
```
Do a dry-run first, then apply if satisified. Also there's a prebuilt prom dashboard: /dashboards/kv-eviction-top-prefixes

oncall-bot: Alert suppressed: router-alert-eu-central-surge for 10m due to manual scaling. Reminders will resume if metrics cross thresholds.

jordan_p: customer comms note: support already opened tickets for top 3 affected customers. SRE -> provide ETA before we escalate to AE outreach. Current ETA: 30-45m for stabilization, variable if new hotspots pop up.

lee: temporary fallback plan if eu-central saturates: enable model-variant fallback for heavy tenants. config snippet:
```
redwoodctl model fallback enable --tenant tenant-42 --from=base-1.0 --to=base-1.0-quantized --rules=latency>600
```
This reduces GPU memory but may change output characteristics — coordinate with PM/CS.

sam: taking note. gaps: secondary coverage for overnight could be thin (only one infra engineer on call). @maria_s can you confirm if infra can escalate to on-call infra team after 30m?

maria_s: infra confirmed standby. if we need shard add -> ping infra pager (infra-oncall). I'm adding that to the incident notes.

alex_k: logging the mitigations in the incident doc. Also starting a short eval run to detect quality regressions if we enable quantized fallback. command:
```
/eval/run quick-check --tenant tenant-42 --variant quantized --samples 50
```

sam: OK I'm primary. Handoff checklist I'm adding here for whoever takes over: - active alerts list - mitigations applied (routing weight change, proxy scale, batch lowering, tenant quotas) - runbook links - infra contact (infra-oncall) - customer tickets. If anything new pops, escalate to SEV1.

maria_s: thanks. I'll be reachable but heading offline in 20m. leaving pager to sam and jordan. Please update the thread with any changes. :thumbsup:

lee: FYI — keeping eviction dry-run ready. if evictions continue after another 15m I'll execute the rebalance and post results here.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-4721 update: last state change 2309004321 by jordan_p. Next automated review in 15m.

sam: noted. anyone picking secondary for the night shift? I'll mark jordan_p as secondary for next 4h. @jordan_p confirm?

jordan_p: confirmed. I'll take secondary for 4h and handle infra escalations if needed.

alex_k: leaving final note — priority: avoid broad tenant throttles; prefer targeted tenant overrides and routing weights. keep customer comms conservative. handing off now. good luck.
